questions.stem: What must the passenger safety briefing under the Small Vessel Regulations cover about stability?
options: The effect of the movement and grouping of passengers on the stability of the vessel
The vessel's KM and KG figures
The IS Code criteria for the vessel
How to incline the vessel
questions.explanation: Section 401(1)(e) lists the effect of the movement and grouping of passengers on stability as a briefing item. Passengers do not need the numbers; they need to know why they should not all rush to one rail.

questions.stem: A crowd of passengers goes up to an upper deck and then moves to one rail. Which two effects do they have on the vessel?
options: Going up lowers G, and moving sideways has no effect
Going up has no effect, and moving sideways raises G
Going up raises G (cutting GM), and moving to one side shifts G sideways (causing a list)
Both movements only increase the displacement
questions.explanation: Weight moved higher raises G; weight moved sideways shifts G off the centreline. Together they produce a bigger list than the sideways movement alone, because the smaller GM gives a larger angle for the same shift.

questions.stem: Ten passengers weighing 80 kg each (0.8 t in all) move 2.0 m to one side of a 20 t vessel with GM 0.40 m. What is the list (tan(list) = GG1 / GM)?
options: About 11.3 degrees
About 5.7 degrees
About 0.2 degrees
About 21.8 degrees
questions.explanation: GG1 = 0.8 x 2.0 / 20 = 0.08 m. tan(list) = 0.08 / 0.40 = 0.20, and the list is 11.3 degrees. 0.2 is the tangent, not the angle; 5.7 degrees comes from dividing by 0.80 as GM.

questions.stem: Under the Small Vessel Regulations, what must the owner and operator of a vessel other than a pleasure craft ensure about stability?
options: That GM is at least 0.15 m at all times
That the vessel has a stability booklet in every case
That passengers do not exceed 12 in number
That the vessel has adequate stability and structural strength to safely carry out its intended operations, and the owner must show this when the Minister asks
questions.explanation: Sections 601(2) and 716 set the standard as adequate for the intended operations. The regulation does not set a GM figure; how stability is shown depends on the vessel's size and the applicable standard.

questions.stem: Who must inform the Minister of a major modification, and what counts?
options: The master; only a change of engine counts
The owner of a vessel other than a pleasure craft; a change that affects watertight integrity or stability counts
The crew; any repair counts
Nobody; this is optional
questions.explanation: Section 710 puts the duty on the owner, and a major modification includes any change that affects watertight integrity or stability.

questions.stem: For larger certificated vessels, which stability standard do the Vessel Certificates and Equipment Regulations require?
options: The Collision Regulations, Rule 7
Compliance with Part B of the 2008 IS Code as modified by the Canadian modifications in TP 7301
A rolling period of less than the beam
No standard; the master decides
questions.explanation: Section 101 refers to Part B of the 2008 IS Code as modified by TP 7301 (December 2023). Whether these regulations apply to a particular vessel depends on its size and operation, so check.

questions.stem: As quoted in this lesson (and not verified in the code itself), which is among the 2008 IS Code general GZ criteria?
options: Area under the GZ curve to 40 degrees of at most 0.09 m.rad
Maximum GZ below 25 degrees
Initial GM of at most 0.15 m
Area under the GZ curve to 40 degrees (or to the downflooding angle if less) of at least 0.09 m.rad
questions.explanation: The quoted criteria are minimums: 0.055 m.rad to 30 degrees, 0.09 m.rad to 40 degrees or the downflooding angle if smaller, 0.03 m.rad between 30 and 40, GZ at least 0.20 m at 30 degrees or more, angle of maximum GZ at least 25 degrees, and GM at least 0.15 m. They are floors, not ceilings.

questions.stem: In an inclining experiment on a 20 t vessel, a 0.4 t weight is moved 2.5 m across the deck and the list gives tan(heel) = 0.10. What GM does this give?
questions.explanation: GM = w x d / (displacement x tan(heel)) = 0.4 x 2.5 / (20 x 0.10) = 1.0 / 2.0 = 0.50 m. 0.05 divides by the wrong value, and 5.0 forgets the displacement.

questions.stem: Which best describes a stability booklet or notice on a vessel?
options: An optional guide that the master may ignore
A document that replaces the master's judgement in all weather
A document supplied by a competent person that sets operating limits; the master must operate within them and keep a copy aboard
A record of the vessel's repairs
questions.explanation: Under the pattern in the Fishing Vessel Safety Regulations (ss. 3.57 to 3.6), a competent person provides the booklet or record of stability and the notice, a copy is kept aboard, and the master operates within the limits and makes sure the crew know the notice.
